assumptions_made: Used synthetic data generation instead of the provided Hugging Face dataset because the experiment requires specifically grouped observations with configurable between-group and within-group variance, which the persona chat dataset does not provide
Assumed a simple 5-group structure with 20 observations per group for computational tractability
Used a simplified shrinkage estimator rather than implementing the full James-Stein estimator due to time constraints
Set 1000 replicates per heterogeneity level to ensure stable variance estimates within the time budget
Used fixed within-group variance of 0.5² and varied between-group variance through the heterogeneity parameter
Assumed normal distribution of errors for analytical simplicity

results.hypothesis: Test whether a hierarchical estimator has lower variance than a pooled estimator under group heterogeneity.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: The pooled estimator at the same heterogeneity level.
results.success_criteria: The shrinkage estimator has lower variance at every heterogeneity level without coverage dropping below 0.90.
results.notes: At heterogeneity level 0.25, pooled coverage (0.5750) is below 0.90. At heterogeneity level 0.25, shrinkage coverage (0.5730) is below 0.90. At heterogeneity level 0.5, pooled coverage (0.7530) is below 0.90. At heterogeneity level 0.5, shrinkage coverage (0.7550) is below 0.90. At heterogeneity level 0.75, pooled coverage (0.8960) is below 0.90. At heterogeneity level 0.75, shrinkage coverage (0.8960) is below 0.90.
results.methodological_validity: mixed real and synthetic inputs — findings are NOT interpretable as evidence; the synthetic inputs are listed in data_provenance.json
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
